items.title: Can you believe it? An investigation into the impact of retraction source credibility on the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we found...
judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect refers to the finding that people often continue to rely on misinformation in their reasoning even if the information has been retracted.
judge.reason: O resumo confirma que dois experimentos manipularam confiabilidade e expertise da fonte de retratação, mediram a dependência da desinformação e a crença na retratação, e os achados principais correspondem integralmente ao extraído.

items.title: Does explaining the origins of misinformation improve the effectiveness of a given correction?

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we examined whether a correction that explained misinformation as originating either from intentional deception or an unintentional error was more effective than a correction that only identified the misinformation as false.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often has a continuing influence on event-related reasoning even when it is clearly and credibly corrected; this is referred to as the continued influence effect.
judge.reason: O achado extraído é suportado pelo resumo, que afirma que 'informar as pessoas sobre a causa que levou à apresentação de desinformação, seja deliberada ou acidental, pode não ser uma estratégia de correção eficaz além de afirmar que a informação é falsa'.

items.title: Don’t believe them! Reducing misinformation influence through source discreditation

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we tested whether immediate source discreditation could reduce people’s subsequent reliance on fictional event-related misinformation.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often continues to influence people’s reasoning even after it has been corrected.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga diretamente o efeito de influência continuada da desinformação, com experimentos que manipulam correção e descrédito da fonte. O método extraído corresponde ao resumo e o achado principal é sustentado pelo trecho literal.

items.title: Exploring factors that mitigate the continued influence of misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: Across three studies, we evaluated the relative contribution of three factors (i.e., targeting the misinformation, providing an alternative explanation, and relative importance of the misinformation content) to the reduction of the CIE.
judge.evidence_topic: The term “continued influence effect” (CIE) refers to the phenomenon that discredited and obsolete information continues to affect behavior and beliefs.
judge.reason: O achado extraído reflete exatamente o trecho do resumo que menciona redução consistente pela provisão de alternativa e eliminação sob certas condições com combinação de elementos.

items.title: Vaccination against misinformation: The inoculation technique reduces the continued influence effect

judge.evidence_empirical: inoculated participants relied on misinformation less when the correction came from a highly credible source.
judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect of misinformation (CIE) is a phenomenon in which certain information, although retracted and corrected, still has an impact on event reporting, reasoning, inference, and decisions.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada usando experimento com participantes humanos e materiais aparentemente neutros, e o resumo confirma integralmente o achado extraído.

items.title: Examining the role of information integration in the continued influence effect using an event segmentation approach

judge.evidence_empirical: Experiments 1 and2 emploeyed spatial event segmentation boundaries in an attempt to manipulate the ease with which a retraction can be integrated into a participant's mental event model.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation regarding the cause of an event often continues to influence an individual's event-related reasoning, even after they have received a retraction. This is known as the continued influence effect (CIE).
judge.reason: The abstract clearly states the CIE topic, reports two experiments, and the extracted finding matches the abstract's conclusion.

items.title: How Stories in Memory Perpetuate the Continued Influence of False Information

judge.evidence_topic: people sometimes continue to use this misinformation in their reasoning, even if they remember that the information is false, which researchers refer to as the continued influence effect

items.title: Can corrections spread misinformation to new audiences? Testing for the elusive familiarity backfire effect

judge.evidence_empirical: This article presents three experiments (total N = 1718)
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often continues to influence inferential reasoning after clear and credible corrections are provided; this effect is known as the continued influence effect.

items.title: Did he or didn’t he? Mixed evidence for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions

judge.evidence_empirical: Here we report three experiments that tested for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions using a non-dynamic impression-formation task... Participants formed an impression of a fictitious person based on a series of behaviour statements.
judge.evidence_topic: Here we report three experiments that tested for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions using a non-dynamic impression-formation task...
judge.reason: O artigo investiga o efeito de influência continuada de informação falsa retratada, utilizando experimentos com participantes humanos e materiais neutros (personagem fictício). O resumo descreve três experimentos e relata achados mistos, exatamente como extraído. O método descrito coincide com o resumo, e o achado principal é integralmente sustentado pelo texto.

items.title: Does Mud Really Stick? No Evidence for Continued Influence of Misinformation on Newly Formed Person Impressions

judge.evidence_empirical: Across four experiments, we investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation. Participants formed an impression of a protagonist, 'John', based on a series of behaviour descriptions, including misinformation that was later retracted.
judge.evidence_topic: investigated the impact of person-related misinformation and its correction on dynamic (moment-to-moment) impression formation ... no evidence for the continued influence of retracted misinformation on person impressions.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda o efeito de influência continuada, com experimentos neutros e dados próprios; o método e o achado extraídos são totalmente consistentes com o resumo.

items.title: The inhibitory impact of collaboration on the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: Experiment 1 explored the general impact of collaboration on the CIE. Experiment 2 further dissected collaboration into turn-taking and free collaboration conditions, assessing their effects on the CIE at various recall intervals. Building on these findings, Experiment 3 delved into the mechanisms driving the differential effects of turn-taking and free collaboration on misinformation correction.
judge.evidence_topic: The continued influence effect (CIE) of misinformation refers to the persistence of misinformation's impact on memory and inference even when individuals are aware of a retraction. This study examined whether collaborative processes affect the CIE.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda diretamente o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) da desinformação, com experimentos envolvendo participantes humanos e materiais neutros. O resumo confirma o estudo empírico com três experimentos e a metodologia descrita corresponde à extraída. O achado principal extraído reflete com precisão os resultados do resumo.

items.title: Belief updating in the face of misinformation: The role of source reliability

judge.evidence_empirical: Across four experiments, we examined how individuals revise their beliefs when confronted with retracted information and varying source credibility.
judge.evidence_topic: Experiment 1 revealed that participants discounted retracted information and reverted to their prior beliefs, in contrast to the Continued Influence Effect commonly reported in the literature.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda diretamente o efeito de influência continuada ao contrastar seus achados com o Continued Influence Effect (critério on_topic atendido). Trata-se de um estudo empírico com quatro experimentos (empirical true). O tipo de estudo e método extraídos ('Estudo experimental (quatro experimentos)' e a descrição) condizem com o resumo (method_ok true). O achado extraído é integralmente sustentado pelo resumo: o Experimento 1 mostrou que os participantes descartaram a informação retratada (sem o efeito de influência continuada) e o Experimento 2 demonstrou que a confiabilidade da fonte influenciou a atualização de crenças. Portanto, finding supported.

judge.evidence_topic: the continued-influence effect (CIE) ... We observed the CIE in all conditions: Participants continued to refer to the misinformation following a correction
judge.reason: O artigo trata diretamente do efeito de influência continuada, com experimentos online usando cenários neutros e medindo referências à desinformação após correção. Relata coleta de dados próprios (Exp. 1A, 1B, 2A, 2B), o método descrito condiz com o resumo, e o achado principal é sustentado pelo trecho do resumo que afirma que o CIE foi observado e as referências foram similares entre formatos de pergunta.

items.title: Executive function and the continued influence of misinformation: A latent-variable analysis

judge.evidence_empirical: Participants completed several measures of EF subcomponents, including those of updating and inhibition, as well as set shifting, and a standard CIE task.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation can continue to influence reasoning after correction; this is known as the continued influence effect (CIE).
judge.reason: O resumo aborda explicitamente o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) e relata um estudo empírico com participantes humanos que realizaram uma tarefa padrão de CIE, medindo raciocínio após correção. O método extraído corresponde ao descrito no resumo, e o achado principal é sustentado diretamente pela afirmação de que 'a função executiva pode predizer a suscetibilidade ao CIE, especialmente o fator de atualização da memória de trabalho'.

items.title: Electrophysiological correlates of the continued influence effect of misinformation: an exploratory study

judge.evidence_empirical: Participants completed a continued-influence task whilst electroencephalographic data were recorded.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often affects inferential reasoning even after it has been retracted, known as the continued influence effect (CIE).
judge.reason: O artigo trata diretamente do efeito de influência continuada (CIE) com um experimento em humanos usando uma tarefa de influência continuada e registros de EEG, enquadrando-se no tema e recorte. O estudo é empírico e o método extraído corresponde ao descrito no resumo. O achado principal ecoa exatamente as conclusões do resumo sobre as diferenças nos ERPs e a interpretação de que a dependência pós-retratação pode decorrer de uma recordação forte da desinformação.

items.title: Do false allegations persist? Retracted misinformation does not continue to influence explicit person impressions.

judge.evidence_empirical: Participants received examples of behaviors that a fictitious person had allegedly engaged in. The set did or did not include a domestic-violence behavior, which subsequently was or was not retracted.
judge.evidence_topic: Corrected misinformation often continues to influence reasoning; this is known as the continued-influence effect (CIE). … The present study tested if a retracted allegation influences person impressions.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda diretamente o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) com estímulos neutros (comportamentos de uma pessoa fictícia), usa delineamento experimental para medir impressões após retratação, o método descrito coincide com o resumo, e os achados extraídos (nenhuma influência explícita; evidência tentativa em medida indireta) estão integralmente sustentados pelo resumo.

judge.evidence_empirical: In two experiments, we found evidence against this hypothesis
judge.evidence_topic: People often continue to rely on misinformation in their reasoning after they have acknowledged a retraction; this phenomenon is known as the continued-influence effect.

É um estudo empírico com dois experimentos (dados próprios). judge.evidence_empirical: One hundred and twenty-nine lay participants completed an adaptation on the traditional continued influence paradigm
judge.evidence_topic: One hundred and twenty-nine lay participants completed an adaptation on the traditional continued influence paradigm, which set out to identify whether it is possible to debunk a piece of common statistical misinformation: inappropriate causal inference based on a correlation.
judge.reason: O artigo aborda o efeito de influência continuada (retractions ... continuing to influence reasoning) com materiais neutros (desinformação estatística comum sobre correlação e causalidade), é um experimento com participantes humanos, o método extraído corresponde ao delineamento descrito no resumo e o achado principal está plenamente respaldado pelo resumo (the data strongly supported the primary hypotheses; efficacy of corrections).

items.title: Combating false information in military situations: Striking the right balance between continued influence effect and overcorrection

judge.evidence_empirical: A total of 61 participants read four military scenarios designed to simulate decision‐making, followed by an assessment of their inferential reasoning. Two of the scenarios presented FI which was later retracted, and the two remaining scenarios did not.
judge.evidence_topic: while others highlight the continued influence effect (CIE), where attitudes persist in alignment with FI. This research aimed to examine the effect of an FI correction within military scenarios.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga diretamente o efeito de influência continuada (CIE) em cenários militares (neutros), usando experimento com participantes humanos que mede raciocínio inferencial após correção, com dados próprios. O método extraído reflete o resumo, e o achado (ausência de CIE e presença de supercorreção) é plenamente sustentado pelo trecho "The results did not reveal any evidence of the CIE, but an overcorrection effect emerged in decision‐making".

items.title: Influence of individual differences in working memory on the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: The results showed that the individual differences in central executive function could significantly affect the CIE, especially for the high-relevant misinformation.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often continues to influence people's cognition even after being retracted (the continued influence effect of misinformation, CIE).

items.title: Influence of individual differences in executive functions of WM on the continued influence effect of misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: The aim of the present study was to verify if there were differences in the continued influence effect with respect to the individual’s EF availability of WM (i.e., inhibition, shifting and updating). The Stroop task, number shifting task and the n-back task were adopted to investigate the three executive functions of inhibition, shifting and updating, respectively. The results showed that differences in inhibition, but not in shifting and updating, had a significant negative effect on the CIE.
judge.evidence_topic: Misinformation often affects people’s cognition and judgment even when they are aware of a retraction; this is known as the continued influence effect of misinformation (CIE).
judge.reason: O resumo afirma que diferenças em inibição, mas não em alternância e atualização, tiveram efeito negativo significativo no CIE, e que o efeito foi menor em indivíduos com alta inibição, o que coincide com o achado extraído.
